research_question: Holding the shared failed candidate, measured state feedback, and budget fixed, does restricting the repair output to the diagnosed stage method change success or cost relative to a complete-module rewrite?
provenance_note: This ablation protocol is deliberately a separate file so the pinned selective_migration_study.json bytes stay unchanged for historical evidence verification.

repair_granularity_ablation.failed_candidate_provenance: The replayed incumbent whose measured align stage claimed completion while official is_cubeA_on_cubeB stayed false; it is the same starting point used by the three method_patch runs in evidence/stackcube_automatic_20261023.
repair_granularity_ablation.paired_sampling_seeds: generation_settings().sampling_seed advanced once per repetition, identical across arms

arms.method_patch: LLM returns only the diagnosed _stage_* method; the harness splices it in and AST-locks every other method. This is the existing selective.py --resume-adapter code path with byte-identical prompts, so the arm reproduces the historical method_patch protocol exactly.
arms.module_rewrite: LLM returns one complete module under the same five-stage interface contract with the same measured evidence; any _stage_* method or __init__ may change; a module semantically identical to a tested candidate is rejected before execution.

identical_across_arms: failed candidate bytes and the replay before repair
repair localization output and measured state feedback content
environment seed, model, temperature, output token limit, request timeout, and max cycles
official success authority and conservative acceptance rules
differs_only_by_design: repair output scope: one spliced method versus one complete module
visible incumbent scope: the method arm sees __init__ and the diagnosed method; the module arm sees the complete module because it must reproduce it
metrics: new-candidate cumulative actions excluding the replayed incumbent actions
